close_reason: Workspace-wide convention — PKIX-* tracker IDs are present in public rustdoc throughout the workspace (e.g. pkix-path/src/lib.rs, pkix-revocation/src/lib.rs). The maintainer has accepted this trade-off; retracting as bikeshedding a decided pattern.
description:
src/async_fetcher.rs:13 (and multiple other files): the module-level rustdoc carries internal beads issue identifiers like 'PKIX-a1yc.10' / 'PKIX-a1yc.7' / 'PKIX-a1yc.5' in publicly-rendered docstrings. These render on docs.rs once the crate publishes and look like opaque internal codes to external readers.

Public rustdoc should communicate to a consumer who has never heard of beads. Internal references belong in commit messages and tracker links, not in the consumer-facing API documentation. The internal tracker IDs have meaning to the maintainer but are a source of confusion for consumers.

Recommendation: strip the PKIX-* references from public rustdoc in src/*.rs files. Keep them in CHANGELOG.md (already done — and that's where they belong for change-tracking) and in commit messages. If a docstring needs to reference a design rationale, link to the bead's URL in the workspace's GitHub repo rather than the bead's ID.

Affected: at minimum src/async_fetcher.rs lines 13, src/cache.rs line 3, 59, src/lib.rs line 63, src/clients/ureq.rs line 161 (PKIX-a1yc.9 - the 'tracked under' comment), and probably more. Grep PKIX-a1yc in src/ to find them all.
title: Module-level rustdoc in async_fetcher.rs mentions PKIX-a1yc.10 — internal tracker ID will leak to docs.rs
